precepts.text: In our afflictions we will seek Him early, so we cry daily to the Lord in repentance until He hear us.
precepts.point: His eye mourneth by reason of affliction; he has called daily upon the Most High and stretched out his hands unto Him. When the Lord turns His face from us, a lot of this stuff is relevant to us today, like the dead bodies laying in the streets of the great city.

note.label: Psalm 88: A Soul Full of Troubles

precepts.why:
“Mine eye mourneth by reason of affliction: Lord, I have called daily upon thee, I have stretched out my hands unto thee.” Hosea shows why the affliction and the daily calling go together: “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.”

The Lord goes back to his place until we acknowledge our offence and seek his face. In our afflictions we will seek him early, so we cry daily to the Lord in repentance until he hear us.

When the Lord turns his face from us, he lays us in the lowest pit, in darkness, and puts our acquaintance far from us. A lot of this stuff is relevant to us today, like the dead bodies laying in the streets of the great city. The way out is what Hosea says: acknowledge the offence, seek his face early, and keep calling daily.

precepts.text: We cry daily to the Lord keeping the commandments and the faith in Christ until He hear us.
precepts.point: His eye mourneth by reason of affliction; he has called daily upon the Most High and stretched out his hands unto Him. When the Lord turns His face from us, a lot of this stuff is relevant to us today, like the dead bodies laying in the streets of the great city.

note.label: Psalm 88: A Soul Full of Troubles

precepts.why:
The psalmist is “shut up” and “cannot come forth”, afflicted with all the Lord's waves, yet he says, “I have called daily upon thee, I have stretched out my hands unto thee.” Solomon prayed for exactly this for Israel in captivity: “Yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives, and repent, and make supplication unto thee in the land of them that carried them captives, saying, We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness”.

That is the supplication of Psalm 88 from the lowest pit. In the land of them that carried us captive we bethink ourselves, repent and say we have sinned. So we cry daily to the Lord, keeping the commandments and the faith in Christ, until he hear us.

precepts.text: There is no work and no devices in the grave; you cannot serve God when you are dead.
precepts.point: He asks whether His wonders shall be known in the dark and His righteousness in the land of forgetfulness. You can't serve God when you're dead.

note.label: Psalm 88: A Soul Full of Troubles

precepts.why:
The psalmist asks, “Wilt thou shew wonders to the dead? shall the dead arise and praise thee?” and “Shall thy wonders be known in the dark? and thy righteousness in the land of forgetfulness?” Solomon answers why he pleads for his life now: “Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might; for there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in the grave, whither thou goest.”

There is no work and no device in the grave. You can't serve God when you're dead. That is why the psalmist begs to be heard while he lives: his lovingkindness is not declared in the grave, nor his faithfulness in destruction. Whatever your hand finds to do for the Most High, do it with your might while you have breath.

precepts.text: For dogs have compassed me; they compassed Christ about as prophesied here.
precepts.point: They came round about him daily like water, dogs have compassed him, like it says in Psalm 22; lover and friend are put far from him and his acquaintance into darkness. These are the prophecies of our forefathers, and this is the real black history, the Most High declaring the end from the beginning to strengthen our faith.

note.label: Psalm 88: A Soul Full of Troubles

precepts.why:
“They came round about me daily like water; they compassed me about together.” Psalm 22 shows who compassed him: “For dogs have compassed me: the assembly of the wicked have inclosed me: they pierced my hands and my feet.”

Dogs have compassed him. They compassed Christ about as prophesied here, and pierced his hands and his feet. The psalmist's cry, “Lord, why castest thou off my soul? why hidest thou thy face from me?”, is the affliction of Christ, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani, my God why are you so far from me. His fierce wrath went over him and his terrors cut him off, like Christ was cut off from the land of the living, with lover and friend put far from him.

These are the prophecies of our forefathers, and this is the real black history: the Most High declaring the end from the beginning to strengthen our faith.

precepts.text: The Lord gave the word; the forefathers wrote down what the Lord said through them.
precepts.point: They came round about him daily like water, dogs have compassed him, like it says in Psalm 22; lover and friend are put far from him and his acquaintance into darkness. These are the prophecies of our forefathers, and this is the real black history, the Most High declaring the end from the beginning to strengthen our faith.

note.label: Psalm 88: A Soul Full of Troubles

precepts.why:
Everything in Psalm 88, the soul cast off, the face hidden, the terrors, the dogs compassing him about, was written before it happened to Christ. How? “God hath spoken once; twice have I heard this; that power belongeth unto God.”

The Lord gave the word; the forefathers wrote down what the Lord said through them. Power belongs unto God, and that includes the power to declare the end from the beginning. That is why these prophecies are the real black history, given to strengthen our faith: what our forefathers wrote was heard from the Most High.

points: The prayer cries day and night before the Most High, asking that his prayer come before Him and that He incline His ear unto his cry, for his soul is full of troubles and his life draws near unto the grave.
